description: Starts a subprocess that replays a preset list of model replies for a named test job, then reads the process output and the recorded entries it wrote. Returns the job's identifier, final state, elapsed time and quiet time, and raises an error when the job never reports an identifier or its record lacks a closing entry.

Chooses the folder to inspect from the option values: a given folder path is used when it exists, otherwise the identifier is checked for safe characters and turned into a path under the standard store. Raises an error when the identifier is missing or malformed, or when the folder does not exist, and returns the absolute folder path.

Looks through the stored sessions in the standard folder and its nested extra folder, picks the newest by identifier, and reports how many entries it holds and how its last record ended. Returns a plain note saying no session exists when the folder is missing or holds nothing usable.

Runs a set of validation tests on a project location: a code-parsing test always, and when the location is this tool's own repository it also tests the character set, documentation, reference listings, knowledge pages, agent instruction files, links, background threads, prompt wording and a quick end-to-end trial. Returns an overall pass flag, the names of the tests that did not pass, every test result, and a list of what the tests did not cover.

Creates a fresh temporary folder, runs a basic end-to-end trial that must complete and a deliberately limited trial that must hit its step cap, then deletes the folder whatever happens. Returns a pass flag and a short note saying which expectation failed, or that both behaved as expected.

Opens an append-only journal file together with a fixed-width lookup file that maps each entry number to its byte position and span, restoring the number of stored items, total bytes and most recent items from what is already on disk. Returns a writer object that gives a time reading, tracks active calls, buffers new entries, and reads any earlier entry back by number after writing out pending bytes.

Carries out one requested operation with an optional artificial pause: it records the request, waits when a pause is set, performs the operation, and records the reply as a rejection or as a normal success. Returns that reply to the caller.

Assembles the full set of callable operations by combining the base operations with groups from sibling modules for knowledge pages, reviewing work, web retrieval, code-structure analysis, version control and row tracking. Derives the callable names, the compact code-facing list and the lookup table from them, and returns the operation list together with the loaded modules.

Writes a reply object as a single serialized line to the output channel after first writing out pending records, then looks up a continuation registered for that reply's identifier and, if one exists, removes it and calls it.

Builds add, list, close and delete functions for each record category, plus a delete function for planning records. Add checks the heading and text and writes a new open record with a fresh identifier and timestamp; list filters records by category and state and returns a plain listing or a none note; close checks the identifier, sequence number and revision id, confirms the revision exists and the record is still open, then marks it closed with the evidence; delete refuses closed records and removes the record file, and the function returns the set of functions.

Starts a background thread that runs a user-supplied script with its declared operations, forwards the script's operation requests to a handler and sends each reply back, and discards the thread's console output. Returns a promise that settles when the script reports completion, fails, or the thread exits, plus a cancel function that ignores later replies and ends the thread.

Returns a handler for writing knowledge entries. It loads the writer module only on the first call, fills in empty defaults for the optional lists and category, passes the fields on to the writer, and returns a success reply carrying the serialized outcome or passes a failure through.

Starts a repeating background monitor that notices when the running build has become outdated. The first check runs after a short delay and later checks run every fixed period; each outdated finding is reported once per combination and handed to a callback, and failures are recorded. Returns a function that cancels the timers and any secondary monitor.

Removes the caller's own identifier from a request's arguments. When the arguments are an object and the identifier matches, it deletes the top-level copy unless the tool's input schema declares that field, and it also strips matching entries from a nested object. Returns a cleaned copy, or the original arguments when they are not an object or the identifier is not text.

Adds one code-execution endpoint to the protocol host. It accepts a source string plus optional identifier, working folder, reply size limit, parsing flag, timeout and envelope settings, runs the source as an async function with the bound operations and a collector for printed text, and returns that text together with any picture data. On an exception it records the failure in a journal and returns the replies gathered so far, with the failure noted.

Reads the last-used project location from a file in the tool's data folder, trims it, and returns it only when it is still the top folder of a version-control repository. Returns nothing when the file cannot be read or the location is no longer the top folder of a repository.

Shrinks an over-long file read result so its text fits the reply size limit. It finds, by binary search, the longest prefix of text rows that still fits, sets the first and last positions, the number returned and the number available, a more-to-come flag, a byte-clipped flag and the next position, and falls back to clipping one over-long row by characters; it returns the trimmed result, or the original when it already fits or is not a file read.

Recovers a clearer failure text for a failed result that lacks one of its own: when its output text parses as a serialized object holding a non-empty failure string, that string is copied in. Otherwise the result is returned unchanged.

Fills in the next starting position on a cut-short list result that lacks one: when the result is flagged as cut short and has no next position, it sets that position to the starting position plus the number returned, provided that number is positive. Otherwise the result is returned as it was.
Reads the machine-wide startup lock record and returns it, or nothing when the read fails.

Attaches a note to an outgoing reply: a non-object reply is wrapped together with the note, while an object gets the note under a name chosen so no existing field is overwritten, and the new object is returned.

Decides whether an outdated-state update to a planning record may pass without a human check. It accepts only a closing request whose state is outdated, whose reason text says the claim was disproved, and whose cited evidence id is non-empty and appears in the project's recorded calls; anything else is refused.

Tells the parent process that a handed-over network endpoint is ready by sending its process id and build label, then records that the endpoint was adopted along with its address, socket number and route. Does nothing when no handle is given, and ignores a failed send.

Walks up the chain of ancestor processes from a given process id, up to a hop limit, looking for one whose launch text matches a known host application pattern. Returns the match found, a flag saying whether a host application was located, and the id of any process whose launch text could not be read; it stops on a repeated id, an invalid id or the init process, and reports a dead ancestor when it meets one.

Builds a compact summary of a discovered endpoint, copying its origin, process id, socket, connection type and elapsed time, with an empty placeholder standing in for any missing id, socket or connection type. Returns that summary.

Turns an operation's failure output into a hint block. For an unsupported-value failure it names the offending argument and the callable name to call instead; for a missing-required failure it names the required argument and adds a follow-up call line unless the output already has one. Returns an empty string when the output matches neither kind of failure.

Downloads a verified published build of the helper program, writes it to a temporary file in the tools folder with exclusive creation and executable permission, and checks that the copy reports the expected build label and a published-build flag. A failed check deletes the copy and rethrows; a passing copy replaces the installed helper, records the change, and returns the new label and hash.
Attaches cut-off notice codes to a result and to its nested payload whenever either carries a truncation signal. Returns the updated result, or the input unchanged when it is not an object.

Checks whether the installed server build has a newer published version and fetches it when needed. It honors an opt-out setting, refuses to change frozen or locked builds, skips the check when it ran recently unless an override is passed, compares the installed content hash with the latest remote revision, and returns a status object describing what happened.
Finds which live process holds a listening socket on a given network number, and returns its process id, or nothing when no listener is present or the holder is no longer running.

Publishes a reusable instruction entry for a skill with a given label. It starts with the skill's instructions, adds a list of its helper files when any exist, and on each request appends a live status readout for the requested working folder.

Runs a code search on a remote hosting service through its search command, using arguments planned from the request, and returns a failure reply when the search fails. On success it returns a header with the number of matches, then one line per match giving position, repository, file location, revision id, page address and raw address.
